state.misconception_label: Confuses rest and movement on a distance time graph

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: I have: This graph shows how far Fido the dog is from his home. What might the negative-sloping section represent? ![A graph with time (secs) on the horizontal axis and distance (m) on the vertical axis. The graph starts at the origin, travels in a straight line up and right, travels horizontally, then travels in a straight line down and right back to the x-axis. ](). I got Fido has fallen asleep because I'm not sure I worked it out the right way.

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: Let me explain the correct method, and then we will work through an example together. Can you describe what rest and movement represent on a distance-time graph?

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: Um, I think rest is when the line is flat, like horizontal? But I'm not really sure what that means... does that mean Fido isn't moving? And then movement would be when the line goes up or down?

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: Let me explain the correct method, and then we will work through an example together. Rest on a distance-time graph does indeed indicate no movement, as the distance remains constant. Movement, on the other hand, is shown by the line going up or down, indicating a change in distance from the starting point.

score.justification_pass1: The teacher provides mathematically correct explanations but merely tells the student the answers rather than addressing why they confused rest with the negative slope, and the student shows understanding of rest/movement concepts in Turn 2 but never gets to apply this to resolve their original misconception about the negative slope representing sleep.
score.justification_pass2: While the teacher attempts to explain directly and check understanding, they repeat the exact same opening phrase in both turns and fail to provide the promised worked example or comprehensively address the original question about the negative-sloping section.
